iOS 27.3 launches soon with a key change: certain advanced AI features will have daily usage limits. In an article posted on X, leaker pdfu details how this new system works.

Here’s what to expect from iOS 27.3’s usage limits for advanced Apple Intelligence features

When iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and iPadOS 27.3 arrive next month, Apple will implement usage limits for advanced AI features.

Some Apple Intelligence capabilities will continue having unlimited use—mainly ones that run locally. But for server-based features that use Private Cloud Compute (PCC), users will have daily allowances on a per-device basis.

Apple has shared some official word on how usage limits work, but many of the finer details haven’t been publicized yet. However, leaker pdfu has discovered a lot about the behind-the-scenes rules governing usage limits. Many were shared this week in an article posted on X.

For example, here’s each feature’s “standard device limit” in daily tokens per pdfu:

  • Siri AI: 20 tokens
  • Image Playground, generative Photos edits: 10 tokens
  • Shortcuts AFM Cloud model: 5 tokens
  • Shortcuts AFM Cloud Pro model: 0 tokens, but iCloud+ 200 GB plan has 5 tokens
  • Apple Foundation Model via PCC in third-party apps: 5 tokens

As explained in pdfu’s article, token usage depends on the complexity of requests. He writes:

Not all features make the same number of requests. Generating one image in Image Playground, or a single query to the AFM 3 Cloud model in Shortcuts, consumes one token. Siri AI requests may make multiple connections to PCC, as server models make tool calls and receive results. Here’s a timeline of how the query “Find a bookshop near me that’s open right now” uses 2 Siri tokens:

  • The request gets sent to the AFM Cloud planner. 1 token used.
  • The planner returns a call to the “find” tool: “bookshop near me open right now.”
  • While the search is ongoing, Siri opens a session with the AFM 3 Cloud Pro planner. 1 token used.
  • Results from the “find” tool call are sent to the Pro planner, which generates the final response.

    • Apple previously detailed how iCloud+ subscribers will get expanded limits on these features. For example, pdfu confirms that an iCloud+ 2TB plan includes 100 daily tokens for Siri AI, 5x the standard limit of 20.

    It’s also worth noting that not all Siri AI requests will use tokens—only “advanced” requests. If you’re interested in reading more, pdfu also recently outlined what counts as an “advanced” Siri request, which you can read here.

    Do you expect these usage limits in iOS 27.3 to be a problem for you? Let us know in the comments.
